facts.statement: Adelolophus is a genus of crested duck-bill dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Utah.
facts.quote: Adelolophus (meaning "unknown crest") is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaur (a crested "duck-bill") from Upper Cretaceous rocks in the U.S. state of Utah.

facts.statement: The only known species is A. hutchisoni, known solely from a broken upper jawbone.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is A. hutchisoni; the type specimen consists only of a broken maxilla.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places it within the tribe Parasaurolophini, which includes tube-headed lambeosaurs.
facts.quote: phylogenetic analysis confirms this, finding it in Parasaurolophini (tube-headed lambeosaurs).

facts.statement: It lived in a wet environment near the sea that experienced arid seasons.
facts.quote: It would have lived in a wet environment, bordering on the sea but with a more arid season during some times of the year.

facts.statement: The genus name means "unknown crest" because the fossil does not show the crest that is typical for its relatives.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek α~, "not", δηλόω, "to show" and λόφη, "crest", referring to the known anatomy of the species not showing the presumed crest.

facts.statement: The species name honors John Howard Hutchison, who discovered the specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name is in honor of Hutchison, who discovered the specimen.

facts.statement: The triangular shape of the single known bone, a maxilla, identifies it as a lambeosaur, a type of dinosaur with large hollow head crests.
facts.quote: The anatomy of the only known bone, the maxilla (part of the upper jaw, bearing teeth), is identifiable as that of a lambeosaur (a type of dinosaur which possessed large, hollow head crests) based on features such as its triangular shape.

facts.statement: It has a large, elevated triangular process near the back of the jawbone that connects to the palatine bone, unlike the smaller and lower version found in other lambeosaurs.
facts.quote: Near the back end of the maxilla, another distinguishing trait of Adelolophus is its large, elevated palatine process (a triangular that connects to the palatine bone); in other lambeosaurs, it is smaller and lower on the maxilla.

facts.statement: It possesses a unique, thickened ridge running from the jaw joint to the palatine process, a feature not seen in other lambeosaurs.
facts.quote: Running from the jugal articulation to the palatine process, Adelolophus possesses a unique, thickened ridge, also unique among lambeosaurs.

facts.statement: A 2021 study found it to be a member of the tribe Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: A 2021 study by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues included Adelolophus in a phylogenetic analysis (test of its relation to other hadrosaurs) and found it to be a member of the tribe Parasaurolophini.

facts.statement: A more recent study placed it as a close relative to the unusual dinosaur Tlatolophus.
facts.quote: A more expansive study reinforced the position within Parasaurolophini, placing it sister to the unusual Tlatolophus.

facts.statement: It lived during the early Campanian age in the Upper Member of the Wahweap Formation.
facts.quote: Adelolophus pertains to the Upper Member of the Wahweap Formation, which is dated to the early Campanian age.

facts.statement: Its environment was a tidal estuary with meandering rivers and brackish water influenced by the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The environment of the Upper Member was tidal, characterized by meandering rivers. Compared to the lower members, the Upper Member had a more marine influence, caused by the encroaching Western Interior Seaway. This created an estuarine environment with brackish water.

facts.statement: It shared its habitat with fish such as sturgeon, gar, and the large bowfin fish Melvius.
facts.quote: Fish present include indeterminate sturgeon and gar specimens, as well as better remains of the large bowfin fish Melvius.

facts.statement: It lived alongside abundant turtles of the extinct baenid family, including Arvinachelys, Denazinemys, and Neurankylus.
facts.quote: Turtles of the extinct baenid family are abundant at the site; these include Arvinachelys, Denazinemys, Neurankylus, and additional remains not identifiable to the level of species.

facts.statement: It shared its habitat with the ceratopsid dinosaur Machairoceratops.
facts.quote: Ceratopsid dinosaur Machairoceratops is also from the Upper Member.

facts.statement: It belongs to the tribe Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: tribus: Parasaurolophini

facts.statement: Adelolophus hutchisoni is the only known species of the extinct ornithischian hadrosaur genus Adelolophus.
facts.quote: Adelolophus hutchisoni (gr. "cresta desconocida de Howard Hutchison") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Adelolophus de dinosaurio ornitisquio hadrosáurido

facts.statement: Adelolophus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 77 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 77 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Adelolophus is known from an isolated partial maxilla with unique features but similarities to Parasaurolophus and Velafrons.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un maxilar parcial aislado, con rasgos únicos, pero con similitudes con Parasaurolophus y Velafrons, según los autores

facts.statement: Adelolophus was described by Terry Gates and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: Adelolophus fue descrito por Terry Gates et. al en 2014

facts.statement: The genus name Adelolophus means "unknown crest" in Greek, and the species name honors Dr. Howard Hutchison, who found the specimen.
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva del griego adelo, άδηλο por "desconocido" o "incierto" y lophos, λοφος por "cresta", el de la especie hace referencia al Dr. Howard Hutchison, quien encontró el espécimen

facts.statement: Researchers interpreted Adelolophus as the oldest known lambeosaurine in North America, dating to approximately 78 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los autores interpretaron que Adelolophus es el más antiguo de los lambeosaurinos conocidos de América del Norte, de aproximadamente 78 millones de años

facts.statement: John Howard Hutchison and colleagues collected fossils at the site in 1999 based on earlier reports by Howard D. Zeller.
facts.quote: La información reportada por Zeller sería utilizada por John Howard Hutchison y colegas para regresar allí y recolectar fósiles en 1999

facts.statement: The maxilla was first reported in 2013 in a scientific article by Terry Gates and colleagues.
facts.quote: Esta maxila fue reportada por primera vez en 2013, en un artículo científico por Terry Gates y colegas

facts.statement: The holotype is UCMP 152028, an incomplete right maxilla with both ends broken.
facts.quote: El holotipo es el UCMP 152028, una maxila derecha incompleta con ambos extremos rotos

facts.statement: The original study noted the exact locality was unknown, making the assignment to the Upper Member tentative based on surrounding rock matrix.
facts.quote: El estudio señaló que la localidad exacta del espécimen era desconocida, lo que hacía su referencia al Miembro Superior tentativa, simplemente supuesta por la matriz de roca que había rodeado el espécimen

facts.statement: A 2016 study by Hutchison and Patricia A. Holroyd clarified the type locality to the lower part of the Upper Member.
facts.quote: La localidad tipo sería aclarada por un estudio de 2016 realizado por Hutchison y Patricia A. Holroyd, confirmando que provenía del extremo inferior del Miembro Superior

facts.statement: Unique morphological traits distinguish Adelolophus as a distinct genus despite its fragmentary nature.
facts.quote: Varios rasgos morfológicos únicos diagnostican a Adelolophus como un género distinto, a pesar de su naturaleza fragmentaria

facts.statement: The anatomy of the only known bone, the upper jaw maxilla, is identifiable as that of a lambeosaurine dinosaur.
facts.quote: La anatomía del único hueso conocido, el maxilar, parte de la mandíbula superior, que lleva los dientes, es identificable como la de un lambeosáurido

facts.statement: Among its relatives, Adelolophus's anatomy is more similar to parasaurolophines (tube-headed lambeosaurines) than to lambeosaurines (helmet-headed lambeosaurines).
facts.quote: Entre sus parientes, su anatomía es más similar a la de los parasaurolofínidos, lambesaurinos con cabeza de tubo, que a la de los lambeosaurínidos, lambeosaurios con cabeza de casco

facts.statement: Adelolophus differs most prominently from other taxa in its very high medial wall, a crest located along the upper middle edge of the bone.
facts.quote: Se diferencia más prominentemente de otros taxones en su pared medial muy alta, una cresta situada a lo largo del borde medio superior del hueso

facts.statement: The dorsal process, an upward bone extension, is more similar to parasaurolophines, being relatively rounded rather than sharply pointed as in lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: El proceso dorsal, una extensión ósea hacia arriba, es nuevamente más similar al de los parasaurolofínidos, siendo relativamente redondeado en lugar de agudamente afilado como en los lambeosaurínidos

facts.statement: Near the posterior end of the maxilla, a distinctive feature of Adelolophus is its large and elevated palatine process, a triangle connecting to the palatine bone.
facts.quote: Cerca del extremo posterior del maxilar, otro rasgo distintivo de Adelolophus es su gran y elevado proceso palatino, un triángulo que se conecta al hueso palatino

facts.statement: From the jugal articulation to the palatine process, Adelolophus possesses a unique and thickened crest, also unique among lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Adelolophus, que va desde la articulación yugal hasta el proceso palatino, posee una cresta única y engrosada, también única entre los lambeosaurios

facts.statement: The shape of the lower edge of the bone along the tooth row is drastically different from other North American relatives like Parasaurolophus, being rough with protuberances instead of the usual smooth condition.
facts.quote: La forma del borde inferior del hueso, a lo largo de la hilera de dientes, es drásticamente diferente de otros parientes norteamericanos, incluido Parasaurolophus, es rugoso y tiene protuberancias, en lugar de la condición lisa más habitual

facts.statement: Adelolophus is a member of the lambeosaurine subfamily of the Hadrosauridae family.
facts.quote: Adelolophus es miembro de la subfamilia lambeosaurina de la familia Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Close relatives of Adelolophus would have included Parasaurolophus and Charonosaurus.
facts.quote: Los parientes cercanos habrían incluido Parasaurolophus y Charonosaurus

facts.statement: Adelolophus belongs to the Upper Member of the Wahweap Formation, dating to the beginning of the Campanian epoch.
facts.quote: Adelolophus pertenece al Miembro Superior de la Formación Wahweap, que data del inicio de la época del Campaniano

facts.statement: The environment of the Upper Member was tidal, characterized by meandering rivers.
facts.quote: El ambiente del Miembro Superior era de mareas, caracterizado por ríos serpenteantes

facts.statement: This created an estuarine environment with brackish water.
facts.quote: Esto creó un ambiente estuarino con agua salobre

facts.statement: Despite a generally humid climate, there would have been a dry season.
facts.quote: A pesar del clima generalmente húmedo, habría existido una temporada seca

facts.statement: The ceratopsian dinosaur Machairoceratops is also from the Upper Member.
facts.quote: El dinosaurio ceratópsido Machairoceratops también es del Miembro Superior

facts.statement: The time range for Adelolophus is the Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Adelolophus is Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Adelolophus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Adelolophus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of Adelolophus is Adelolophus hutchisoni.
facts.quote: Type species: Adelolophus hutchisoni
